body: I'll have to take a closer look, but from the description, it looks this may be due to the nested schema (nested columns are currently not supported).

Yes there are definitely nested columns, BigQuery uses them pretty heavily.

What is involved in supporting nested columns? It is a pretty crucial feature as more and more big data platforms are pushing it as a more efficient storage method and it really helps with data modelling!

Even if it is something as simple as having the ability to un-nest them?

I should be able to take a closer look on monday. For simple nesting, we should be able to unnest columns by creating new columns such as "structX.fieldstructY.fieldZ" (this should already be supported in the cudf parquet/orc readers, not sure about avro). For more complex nesting, such as lists of structs, we need true nesting support in cudf.

That would be fantastic, to give you an idea of scale this dataset is 86GB with nested compressed avro, it would probably be > 1TB as unnested CSV.
If we can do this on the fly that represents a significant efficiency gain :)

Yeah, the problem is the "meta" column with the "array" type: it seems to be an array-of-records:
`{"name":"meta","type":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"record","namespace":"root","name":"Meta","fields":[{"name":"k","type":["null","string"]},{"name":"v","type":["null","string"]}]}}}`
If it was just a record, we should be able to de-nest it, but as a list, I don't think there is an easy way to do that.
However, one thing we might be able to do is at least parse the full schema such that we could load all the other columns, in case this helps.

Btw, I'm surprised to see AVRO being used for such a large dataset: even though it is more efficient than CSV, avro still requires walking through the full 86GB even if a smaller subset is needed (even though it allows fast skipping of blocks, avro doesn't provide random access, unlike stripes/rowgroups in ORC/parquet)

If there is an option to leave the column as a Json blob that would also be fine (skip column or something of that sort?) The meta column is really just a "catch all" for anything extra in the schema. Alternatively if its possible to create new fields in the schema such as Meta.1.name, Meta.1.type, Meta.2.name, Meta.2.type or equivalent.

I wouldn't use Avro normally for this but its all BigQuery supports for export when there are nested columns (either that or JSON). 

In an ideal world it would export ORC / Parquet but Google doesn't seem to want to support that, so I am only left with the option of exporting in some format to then re-convert to ORC/Parquet (which I think would be a good fit for cuDF rather than spinning up an expensive cluster).

I am going to do an export in CSV which will require me to flatten the schema manually (pain when there are this many nested fields - I excluded about 10 other nested fields from this Avro sample), but if there can be a way to process these Avro files directly that would save me hours each time I need to do this (which is often!)

Alternatively - what about using some kind of SerDe? That seems to be a common way to deal with Avro? That way the user can define how each field is Deserialised and takes away the common "One size fits all"?
Thanks. Same issue with "Cannot parse metadata" on certain nested json avros
Hi, is there any workaround available which can read nested json data in avro files with cuDF?
Not to my knowledge, unless you can remove the lists and/or more-than-1-deep nested columns.
Would it help if the reader was able to load the columns it supports while discarding unsupported lists ?
Thanks! Yes, that would be helpful.  As an alternative, would it be possible to set and convert the problem nested / array type columns to a "string" type?

Looking at this file in particular, it looks like the only problem is the array type: we can de-nest all columns, but without list support in cudf, there are only 3 options I can think of at the moment, in order of increasing complexity:
1. Drop array columns, allowing loading of other columns (everything except the 'meta' column here)
2. Drop everything except the first entry in the array (only the 1st meta entry would be stored in the meta.k and meta.v columns).
3. In the case of array of strings, we could concatenate multiple string entries, adding a ',' separator (this would only work for strings, as is the case here), so no data is dropped.
I'm thinking of starting with option 1, and go from there.

Option 1 turned out simpler than I thought, but options 2 and 3 would require a significant amount of throw-away work (the implementation in PR #4377 technically supports loading the array-of-struct meta column if explicitly requesting all the columns by name, where the result would contain only the last {meta.k,meta.v} pair, but if there are multiple null entries in the array it would lead to incorrect null count, with unpredictable results - by default the reader will not load columns of array type)
